answer.rationale: memory_c2 is the only record that directly evidences a supplier switch and its operational aftermath; if it holds, the switch is credible. memory_c1 confirms the incumbent renews stably but does not solve the mandated cost cut, and memory_c3 shows that adding a second source is the durable lever for risk reduction, so the switch is sized as a primary-supply transfer of the constrained component with the incumbent retained on month-to-month for overflow, keeping dual sourcing without committing to a full break. With no buffer and 14 days to expiry, the switch is staged: new vendor takes the first allocation within a week, incumbent covers the remainder under a short-term month-to-month extension, and delivery risk is capped by capping the new vendor's initial volume at the level memory_c2 supports (quick onboarding, accurate invoicing). I will not verify more than one memory because the budget permits only one and memory_c2 alone is sufficient to decide. If verification fails, the fallback is to renew the incumbent on month-to-month and escalate the cost target to finance rather than absorb risk.
